objective: Cross-route, per-file residual source-asset report: which specific external files the built/served site still requests, on which rendered routes, joined to inventory identity and to the replacement manifest's verdict — plus a route-scope default that covers the site instead of "/" alone.
artifactPath: <materialization-run-dir>/report/residual-source-assets.json (e.g. data/<host>/asset-materializations/<run-id>/report/residual-source-assets.json), schema asset-residual-report-v1, written by pnpm assets:qa alongside the existing report/network-qa.json. Per file it carries: normalized url, host, routes[] (route + occurrences), routeCount, occurrences, inventoryId, assetId, slotKeys, replacement{inManifest, classification, status, providedFile, note, manifestFile} and evidence[] (artifact path + record ref). Report-level: routeScope, inputs (the three joined artifacts), counts (incl. invisibleAtRootOnly), byHost, files[] sorted most-rendered first. A second, package-level per-file view (no inventory join available there) is now also carried on the production QA report as routeCensus[].externalUrls + residualRequestFiles[].

limitations: No real `pnpm assets:qa` run was executed. Doing so requires a browser census over a live template app AND would write into an existing data/<host>/asset-materializations/<run-id>/report/ directory, which this wave forbids. The report is proven by the fixture census in smoke:assets plus a read-only dry run over the historical stripe artifacts (output kept in the scratchpad).

Route scope is only as complete as the template run's site-map.json — representative routes per page family, not every URL of the source site. A residual asset that renders only on a non-represented member page is still invisible; the artifact records its scope, source and any --max-routes truncation so the gap is legible rather than silent.

Cost: the census now loads 2 browser pages per route (baseline + independent). The stripe template run has 20 routes, i.e. ~40 page loads where it used to be 2. --max-routes bounds it and the truncation is recorded in the artifact.

The census sees what headless Chromium at 1440x900 requests after the existing settle + full-page scroll pass. Viewport-conditional or interaction-only assets can still be missed; this change widens ROUTE coverage only.

The inventory join is exact-URL (fragment stripped, query kept). A residual request whose CDN transform query differs from the URL the inventory recorded reports inventoryId null. That is deliberate — a path/basename fallback would be a guess — but it means unjoined does not always mean unknown-to-the-lineage.

The production-QA per-file view (residualRequestFiles) carries no inventory id or replacement status: the deployment package ships neither artifact. It is a locator, and the assets:qa report remains the joined one.

residualRenderedUrlCount, which feeds the replacement-required preview blocker (src/production/run.ts:279), is still totals.residualSourceUrls.length. With the wider census it will legitimately grow on the next real build; that is a truer number, not a regression, but it will move the blocker prose.

The `host` divergence between the assets-layer report (hostname) and the production-QA per-file view (host:port) is documented on both fields but NOT unified. Any consumer that joins the two views by host must normalize; in practice real source/CDN hosts carry no port and the two strings are identical, so no on-disk artifact currently differs.

invisibleAtRootOnly is now null when "/" was not measured, but it still says nothing about routes the census never covered at all. A file invisible on every measured route except one is not distinguished from a file the scope simply never looked for — routeScope (source, routes, truncatedTo, discardedExplicitRoutes) remains the only record of what was NOT measured.

The CLI refusal of an empty --routes is proven only at the library boundary (resolveCensusRoutes returns discardedExplicitRoutes, which is the exact condition src/cli-assets-qa.ts:80 branches on). No fixture spawns the assets:qa process itself — no smoke suite in this repo does — so the exit code 1 is asserted by reading, not by execution.

corrections.finding: MINOR (independent verifier, post-PASS): an explicit --routes value that parses to ZERO routes was silently ignored — src/assets/residual-report.ts:96-109 guarded the explicit branch with `if (explicit.length > 0)` and fell through to the site-map branch, so `pnpm assets:qa … --routes " , "` measured 20 routes while the artifact recorded source="template-site-map" with no trace of the discarded override.
corrections.fix: BOTH halves of the option, because they answer different callers. (1) resolveCensusRoutes now records the raw discarded value on the scope as `discardedExplicitRoutes` and appends `(--routes "…" declared no route and was DISCARDED)` to routeScope.note on every fallback branch (site-map, empty-site-map, unreadable-site-map) — a programmatic caller that keeps running still gets honest provenance in the artifact. (2) src/cli-assets-qa.ts:80-87 REFUSES the run: it prints `--routes declared no route: " , " — pass routes as "/,/pricing", or omit --routes to use <siteMapFile>` and exits 1, before the template app is started.
corrections.whyRejectInTheCli: That is the CLI's existing idiom for bad operator input, and the two neighbouring cases are literally adjacent: `--max-routes` non-positive (src/cli-assets-qa.ts:67-71) and a missing --content-run slot-values.json (lines 60-64) both print one `[assets:qa] …` line and set exitCode 1 rather than substituting a default. An operator who typed --routes wants THOSE routes; measuring 20 different ones and telling them afterwards is the wrong trade at a CLI. The library keeps the softer behaviour because resolveCensusRoutes is a pure resolver with a `note`/provenance contract and must stay total — it has no exit code to spend.
